chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there Zakat upon the one who accepts Zakat? He said: 'As for the one who accepts Zakat of wealth, then upon him is Zakat al-Fitr, and he is not required to give Zakat for what he has accepted; and upon the one who accepts al-Fitr, there is no Fitr.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: Al-Fitr (the charity of breaking the fast)
key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (charity of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: Does a person who receives Zakat alms still have to pay Zakat al-Fitr?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinct legal categories of Zakat and Zakat al-Fitr, establishing that receiving one form of alms does not exempt an individual from the obligation of the other. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that Zakat al-Fitr is a personal duty tied to the individual's status as a Muslim capable of fasting, independent of their wealth accumulation from other Zakat sources. It highlights the non-transferable nature of these obligations, ensuring that the spiritual purification associated with Fitr remains a direct responsibility of the recipient.
